title: Copilot Studio: improvements to the agent evaluations experience
summary: Hold: the briefing incorrectly says General quality is the only evaluation method for Microsoft Copilot harness agents. Microsoft now documents several methods and allows up to five per evaluation. The roadmap facts and the listed control paths and operations are supported; the REST call formatting and a checklist-to-table mismatch need minor corrections.

claims.claim: PUT licensing/allocationsV2 using version 2024-10-01 sets the environment's MCSMessages allocation quantity and TenantPool enforcement rule through the printed request properties.
claims.quote: Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put ... -Uri "$apiBaseUrl/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=$apiVersion" ... scope = @{ environmentId = $environmentId } ... entitlementId = "MCSMessages" ... allocation = @{ quantity = 5000 } ... @{ ruleType = "TenantPool"; enabled = $false }
claims.fix: Set controls[1].api.call and the rendered call to 'PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01'. Add to its note: 'The request body sets scope.environmentId and allocatedEntitlements, including entitlementId=MCSMessages, allocation.quantity and enforcementRules with ruleType=TenantPool and enabled=false.' The cited tutorial confirms the operation; the pre-check missed its interpolated URL.

claims.claim: Managing the allocation requires Power Platform Administrator, Global Administrator or an equivalent licensing-and-capacity management role.
claims.quote: Sign in as a user with the **Power Platform Administrator** or **Global Administrator** role, or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.

claims.claim: A published environment-group tenant-draw rule makes the environment setting read-only.
claims.quote: When you publish a rule, it governs every environment in the group. The environment-level setting becomes read-only in the Power Platform admin center, and programmatic requests can't override it.

claims.claim: Attempts to override a published tenant-pool group rule are rejected with TenantPoolLockedByPolicy.
claims.quote: Updates through the Power Platform admin center, Power Platform API, or administration SDKs are rejected with the `TenantPoolLockedByPolicy` error.

claims.claim: Independent management requires changing and republishing the group rule or removing the environment from the group.
claims.quote: Change and republish the rule for the environment group, or [remove the environment from the group](environment-groups#remove-an-environment-from-your-environment-group) to manage the setting independently.

claims.claim: Turning off tenant-pool draw does not prevent continued consumption through a linked pay-as-you-go plan.
claims.quote: If the environment is linked to a pay-as-you-go billing plan, usage can continue through the linked Azure subscription.

claims.claim: Licensing > Copilot Studio > Manage Agents > agent > Set limit > Stop usage is the documented route to the agent monthly-limit stopping control.
claims.quote: go to **Licensing** > **Copilot Studio**. ... Select **Manage Agents**. ... Select the agent, and then select **Set limit**. ... Turn on **Stop usage** if the agent should be turned off when it reaches the limit.

claims.claim: The versioned resource-threshold PUT operation accepts limit and stopIfOverCapacity to configure an environment resource's consumption threshold.
claims.quote: PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/environments/{environmentId}/entitlements/{entitlementId}/resources/{resourceId}/threshold?api-version=2024-10-01 ... limit ... stopIfOverCapacity
claims.fix: Set controls[2].api.call and the rendered call to 'PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/environments/<environment-id>/entitlements/<entitlement-id>/resources/<resource-id>/threshold?api-version=2024-10-01'. Add to the note: 'The request body sets limit and stopIfOverCapacity=true.' Keep the existing general-resource and ID-mapping caveat. The pre-check's literal-placeholder miss is not an endpoint defect.
